title: Week 2: Give it a neck

series.title: Physical AI Lab: Cardboard Robot (4 week course)

summary: Your talking box gets a neck. A second cut-down box, a servo and a lazy-susan bearing let the head turn, a battery pack powers both servos, and the voice agent learns two new function calls: turn its head and look around.
detail: Bring last week's robot. You build a short base with a servo and a 3 inch lazy-susan bearing, sit the head on it, and power both servos from a battery pack while the Pico stays on your laptop. Then switch on the neck in the app and teach your agent when to use it.
outcome: Your robot turns its head and looks around on its own while it talks.
artifact: A two-servo cardboard robot with a turning head, driven by voice-agent function calls.
prereqs: Your robot from Week 1, and a laptop with Chrome.
Everything else is on the table: the neck kit and a battery pack.

slides.title: Week 2: Give it a neck
bullets: Last week: it talks and its mouth moves.
Tonight: the head turns, and it decides when to look around.
Plus your own power bank, so in Week 3 it can go cordless.
slides.note: Have one finished robot look around the room as people sit down.

slides.title: What each robot needs this week
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Week 1, with its Pico, breadboard, power lead and USB cable
☐ 1 more 8×8×8 inch box, cut down to about 3 inches tall
☐ 1 × MG90S micro servo (the neck)
☐ 1 × 3 inch lazy-susan bearing, with 4 small screws
☐ 1 × male-to-female jumper wire (neck signal)
☐ 2 × male-to-male jumper wires (neck power)
☐ 1 × 10,000 mAh power bank with two ports (one USB-C, 20 W or more), charged
Bring: a laptop with Chrome, and your Deepgram key
slides.note: The power bank stays with the robot for the rest of the series: in Week 3 it powers the Pi too. Charge every one the night before. Shared per table: hot-glue gun and glue sticks, a small screwdriver, a box cutter. Helper table: spare servos, jumpers, breadboards and power leads, plus spare Week 1 robots for anyone who missed it. Check every build has its ground jumper before it's powered on.

slides.title: Make the base
bullets: Cut a small hole in the middle of the short box's lid.
Hot-glue the neck servo under the lid by its two tabs, so its shaft pokes up through the hole.
Screw or glue the lazy-susan bearing on top, centred on the shaft.
slides.note: Done when: the bearing spins freely and the servo's shaft sits in the middle of it.

slides.title: Mount the head
bullets: Glue a servo horn to the middle of the head's underside.
Lower the head onto the bearing so the horn pushes onto the servo's shaft.
The bearing carries the weight; the servo only turns it.
slides.note: Done when: turning the head by hand turns the servo, and the head doesn't wobble.

slides.title: Wire and power it
bullets: Neck signal (orange) to GP14, pin 19, right above the mouth wire.
Neck red to the breadboard's + row, neck brown to the − row, next to the mouth servo's.
Everything else stays where it was in Week 1, including the ground jumper to pin 23.
Power lead into the table charger or your power bank. Nothing on pin 40.
The Pico stays plugged into your laptop.
slides.note: The power is the same as Week 1: both servos share the breadboard rails, and the Pico only sends signals. If anyone still has their mouth servo's red on pin 40 from an old build, move it to the + row now. The shared ground matters: without it the servos twitch randomly.

slides.title: Switch on the neck
bullets: Connect the robot like last week.
Open Neck on the Plug in card and tick My robot has a neck servo.
Set Looking left and Looking right, then press Look around.

slides.title: How the head turns
bullets: You ask: "Who is on your left?"
The agent decides to call turn_head with direction "left".
The page turns "left" into an angle (150° by default) and sends it to the Pico, a few degrees at a time.
The Pico moves the neck servo and the head turns. look_around is left, then right, then straight ahead.
slides.note: The servo can point anywhere from 0° to 180°. Looking left and Looking right on the page set the two angles; if the head turns the wrong way, swap them.

slides.title: Teach it when to move
bullets: Your agent now has two new functions: turn_head and look_around.
Ask it to look around. Watch the Tool lines in the transcript.
Edit its personality: when should it turn its head? When it's curious? When someone new talks?
Test it. Does it move at the right moments, or too much?
slides.note: Same idea as last week's weather skill: the agent decides when to call a function, and the page carries it out. Here the function moves something real.

slides.title: Week 3: make it standalone (optional)
bullets: Want your robot to run without your laptop? Bring your own Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 and a USB speakerphone.
Set it up at home first: the steps are on the Week 3 page.
Want it to run longer? There's an optional battery upgrade list on the Week 3 page. Buy it yourself and bring it in.
No Pi? Come anyway. Your robot keeps running from your laptop, and there's a voice studio track for you.
slides.note: Say this twice and put it in the follow-up email: anyone doing the Pi upgrade brings their own Pi and USB speakerphone, and sets the Pi up at home before Week 3. Mention the optional upgrade list too: anyone who wants a bigger battery buys it before Week 3. The free power bank works fine.

flow.title: Turn the head
flow.note: Plug the robot in, connect it, then open Neck on the Plug in card.

troubleshooting: The Pico resets or disconnects when the head moves: a servo is still on the Pico's power. Both red wires go to the breadboard's + row, with the charger or power bank plugged in. The page reconnects on its own once it's back.
The servos twitch or jitter on their own: the breadboard's − row isn't joined to the Pico's GND. Add the ground jumper.
Nothing moves at all: the power bank may have gone to sleep. Press its button, or plug the power lead into the table charger.
The head turns the wrong way: swap the Looking left and Looking right numbers.
The head wobbles or sags: the weight is on the servo, not the bearing. Re-seat the head so it rests on the bearing.
It never turns its head: check My robot has a neck servo is ticked before you press Start talking.
